title: Abstract the transport over UnixListener/UnixStream
description:
THE GATE. The epic measures 21 sites, nearly all in hire-grpc/src/server.rs, that name tokio::net::UnixListener or UnixStream concretely. The socket path, the accept loop and consumer attestation all bottom out in those types, so nothing else in this epic can be attempted first.

hire-grpc/src/socket.rs already carries the ponytail comment naming this as the upgrade path: 'unix domain sockets only | ceiling: Windows needs a named pipe, which this function cannot express | upgrade path: abstract the transport over UnixListener/UnixStream first, then return a platform-tagged endpoint instead of a PathBuf'.

SCOPE IS THE ABSTRACTION ONLY. No named pipe code in this bead, no Windows target. The deliverable is that hire-grpc names a trait rather than a concrete type, with the existing Unix implementation behind it and the test suite unchanged and green. A second implementation is persona-vvs2.4's job.

TWO THINGS THE ABSTRACTION MUST CARRY, or it will need redoing:
  - the PEER IDENTITY of an accepted connection, not just the byte stream.
    consumer_attest.rs reads SO_PEERCRED off the Unix socket; a named pipe
    answers GetNamedPipeClientProcessId instead. If the trait yields only an
    AsyncRead/AsyncWrite, attestation cannot be implemented on either side of
    it. Note the current fail-shut default at hire-grpc/src/service.rs:238-247
    -- a transport that does not attest DENIES -- and keep that property: a
    new transport added later must fail shut, not open.
  - the ENDPOINT, as a platform-tagged value rather than a PathBuf. SPIFFE
    already has the convention: an npipe: endpoint address on Windows against
    unix: elsewhere.

Also here: the single #[cfg(not(unix))] in the whole workspace lives at hire-grpc/src/server.rs:223, and the lock lifetime comment at server.rs:17 ('_lock must stay alive for as long as this server serves') is a flock property that the abstraction must not silently drop -- see persona-vvs2.7.
acceptance_criteria: hire-grpc names a transport trait, not a concrete Unix type; peer identity and endpoint are expressible through it; the Unix implementation is unchanged in behaviour and the suite is green; no Windows code.
